record_scope_reconstruction: Naf River cargo interchange from the Maungdaw area to Teknaf land port, with a contemporary 2025 halt and a May 2026 timber arrival. Teknaf’s Bangladesh terminal can be referenced at its documented entrance. Myanmar reports identify Hainkhali canal and Kanyinchaung jetty without an established common berth coordinate; Yangon/Sittwe coastal shipping and St Martin tourist ferries are excluded.

May 1 timber arrival at Teknaf jetty from Hainkhali canal; no exact coordinates and no general normal-service claim.

Port operator identifies the Naf River trade facility and distinct passenger/cargo jetties.
Government port description pairs Teknaf land port with Maungdaw and locates it five kilometres from Teknaf centre.

sites.evidence_note: The photographer identifies the Teknaf land-port entrance opposite Maungdaw and supplies camera GPS/EXIF; the operator identifies the Naf River freight port and separate cargo/passenger facilities. The nearby St Martin ferry landing and conflicting town-centre Wikipedia coordinates are excluded. Only the Bangladesh terminal is located; Myanmar departure jetty identity is incomplete.

date_scope_check.finding: Geography review only. Current phase bounds, traffic exceptions, uncertain onset, reopening status and >24-hour decision are retained; current map features are not evidence of historical operation.
date_scope_check.qualification: The onset accounts describe different events: Jago News on May 28, 2025 quotes the port general manager saying trade had halted since April 12, while bdnews24 identifies April 12 as the last earlier wooden-boat arrival. Preserve both attributed accounts without treating a last-open observation as an exact closure start or calculating 384 continuous closed days. The exact transition after that arrival is not independently timed. April 14, 2026 was a reopening announcement, not actual return. TBS and BSS confirm the May 1 timber arrival but give different clocks, 13:30 and 13:10; BSS says unloading and customs assessment were still pending. DMG on May 5 reported no additional trip yet. By June 1, DMG via BNI described limited timber exports and small reverse potato/onion flows, mainly through a ULA-linked merchants’ association. That provides a bound for some reverse trade, not its first date, unrestricted private access or normal service. Yangon/Sittwe coastal shipping remains excluded; actor and authorization chronology remains attributed and incomplete. The May 28 contemporary report explicitly describes a 45-day halt, supporting the greater-than-24-hour threshold independently of uncertainty over the exact transition after April 12 and the later restoration sequence. This does not establish uninterrupted closure for every commodity until May 2026.
